examples.text: „Im Sommer ist dieser Teil des Heath an jedem Samstagabend Schauplatz von Konzerten mit wunderbar englischer Atmosphäre: Man sitzt auf Deckchairs oder auch auf Picknickdecken und lauscht bei einem Glas Champagner sehr gepflegt der meist klassischen Musik.“
„Die Schauplätze und die Zeiten, um die es im Gespräch ging, wechselten oft, und doch blieb es beim Thema.“
„Der Norden Afrikas wird während des Zweiten Weltkriegs zum Schauplatz gewaltiger Schlachten zwischen der deutschen Wehrmacht und den angloamerikanischen Alliierten.“

„Selbst als man keine Grabhügel mehr errichtete, dienten die alten Monumente nicht nur als Schauplatz von Spukerzählungen, sondern konnten ganz pragmatisch weiterbenutzt werden: Ein Grabhügel bei Skipsea im Osten des englischen Yorkshire, der aus der Zeit um 500 vor Christus stammt und stolze 85 m Durchmesser und 13 m in der Höhe maß, wurde von den Normannen 1500 Jahre später als Burgberg wiederverwertet.“

translations.source_sense_description: Ort, an dem etwas stattfindet oder stattgefunden hat

glosses: The location of an event that attracts attention.

examples.text: the scene of the crime

glosses: The stage.

examples.text: They stood in the centre of the scene.

glosses: The decorations; furnishings, and backgrounds of a stage, representing the place in which the action of a play is set.

examples.text: to paint scenes
to change the scenes
behind the scenes

glosses: A part of a dramatic work that is set in the same place or time. In the theatre, generally a number of scenes constitute an act.

examples.text: The play is divided into three acts, and in total twenty-five scenes.
The most moving scene is the final one, where he realizes he has wasted his whole life.
There were some very erotic scenes in the movie, although it was not classified as pornography.

Miss Phyllis Morgan, as the hapless heroine dressed in the shabbiest of clothes, appears in the midst of a gay and giddy throng; she apostrophises all and sundry there, including the villain, and has a magnificent scene which always brings down the house, and nightly adds to her histrionic laurels.

glosses: The location, time, circumstances, etc., in which something occurs, or in which the action of a story, play, or the like, is set up.

examples.text: In Troy, there lies the scene.
The world is a vast scene of strife.

glosses: A combination of objects or events in view or happening at a given moment at a particular place.

examples.text: He assessed the scene to check for any danger, and agreed it was safe.
They saw an angry scene outside the pub.
Through what new scenes and changes must we pass!

glosses: A landscape, or part of a landscape; scenery.

examples.text: A sylvan scene with various greens was drawn, / Shades on the sides, and in the midst a lawn.

He turned back to the scene before him and the enormous new block of council dwellings. The design was some way after Corbusier but the block was built up on plinths and resembled an Atlantic liner swimming diagonally across the site.

glosses: An exhibition of passionate or strong feeling before others, creating embarrassment or disruption; often, an artificial or affected action, or course of action, done for effect; a theatrical display.

examples.text: The headmistress told the students not to cause a scene.
The crazy lady made a scene in the grocery store.
Probably no lover of scenes would have had very long to wait or some explosions between parties, both equally ready to take offence, and careless of giving it.

I'm having wicked dreams of leaving Tennessee
Hear Santa Monica, I swear it's calling me
Won't make my mama proud, it's gonna cause a scene
She sees her baby girl, I know she's gonna scream

glosses: An element of fiction writing.
A social environment consisting of an informal, vague group of people with a uniting interest; their sphere of activity; a subculture.

examples.text: She got into the emo scene at an early age.
Indie just isn't my scene.

glosses: A youth subculture popular in the Anglosphere in the 2000s and early 2010s.
A fantasy that is acted out.
To exhibit as a scene; to make a scene of; to display.
To roleplay.
A notice to actors that their performance has ended.

examples.text: Near-synonym: cut!

glosses: A theater, auditorium, arena, or other area designated for sporting or entertainment events.
A neighborhood or near place; the place or county in which anything is alleged to have happened; also, the place where an action is laid, or the district from which a jury comes.

examples.text: The twelve men who are to try the cause must be of the same venue where the demand is made.

glosses: A bout; a hit; a turn.
A stadium or similar building in which a sporting competition is held.

examples.text: With such focus from within the footballing community this week on Remembrance Sunday, there was something appropriate about Colchester being the venue for last night’s game. Troops from the garrison town formed a guard of honour for both sets of players, who emerged for the national anthem with poppies proudly stitched into their tracksuit jackets.

glosses: The place where something happens.

examples.text: The metalworking forum is not the appropriate venue for this discussion about politics.

glosses: Espace généralement décoré où des comédiens, parfois accompagnés d’autres artistes comme des musiciens, jouent un rôle, interagissent.
